prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single objectively “best” roofer for everyone — the best choice depends on your exact neighborhood, your insurance situation, and the contractor’s experience with hail repairs and insurance claims. I can help you find highly rated roofers near you if you tell me your Denver ZIP code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s how to find and pick the best roofer for hail damage:

What matters when choosing a roofer for hail damage
- Experience with hail/ storm damage and insurance claims (knows Xactimate, claim process).
- Proper licensing and liability/workers’ comp insurance (ask for certificates).
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) and transferable warranties.
- Local, established company with verifiable references and long track record.
- Written, itemized estimate and scope of work (materials, layers removed, flashing, permit, cleanup).
- Responsive communication and availability for emergency tarping if needed.

How to find candidates
- Check Google Reviews, BBB, Angi, Yelp for companies near your ZIP code and read recent storm-season reviews.
- Look for manufacturer-certified contractors on GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning websites.
- Ask neighbors or HOA if they’ve had recent hail repairs and who they used.
- Get at least three written estimates.

Questions to ask every roofer
- How long have you been doing hail/storm repairs in Denver?
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you provide CO liability and workers’ comp certificates?
- Are you manufacturer-certified? What warranty do you offer (manufacturer + workmanship)?
- Do you handle the insurance claim and work directly with the adjuster?
- Will you remove old shingles down to deck or do overlays? (Hail usually requires full removal.)
- Who does the work — employees or subcontractors? Who is on-site?
- Do you obtain permits and provide lien waivers and clean-up (magnet sweep for nails)?
- What is the timeline and payment schedule? Any upfront deposit?

Red flags
- High-pressure door-to-door solicitors right after a storm (“we’re from out of town”).
- Cash-only, large up-front payments, or unwillingness to provide written contract.
- Vague scope, no detailed line-item estimate, or refusal to show insurance/ license proof.
- Extremely low price well below other bids.

If you want, tell me:
- Your Denver ZIP code/neighborhood
- Whether you’re filing an insurance claim
I’ll suggest top-rated local roofers to consider and can help you compare any estimates or contracts you receive.
